text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Fifty one criminal suspects refused to be tried by a high court judge they said was notorious for handing down severe penalties and delaying cases. The prisoners face charges ranging from armed robbery to murder.
- The International Red Locusts Control Organisation has put its staff on "full alert" in anticipation of an invasion by the insects.
- Local government workers in the southern city of Livingstone have gone on strike to push for improved pay.
- A total of 1,529 Zambians were arrested locally and a further 22 in foreign countries for trafficking in narcotics in 1996, the drug enforcement comnmission said.
- The Economic Association of Zambia has urged the government to cut Value Added Tax in its 1997 budget, to be announced at the end of the month.
